target: Voici le collègue dont je t'ai souvent parlé.
english: Here is the colleague I've often told you about.
tip: 'Dont' replaces 'de + qui/quoi': 'le collègue dont je t'ai parlé' = whom I told you about (parler de).

target: Si j'avais choisi médecine, je serais médecin maintenant.
english: If I had chosen medicine, I would be a doctor now.
tip: No 'a' before a profession after être: je serais médecin = I'd be a doctor. You only add un when you describe it – un bon médecin.

target: Le cadeau que j'ai reçu m'a fait très plaisir.
english: The gift I received made me very happy.
tip: After 'que', the participle quietly agrees with the noun before it: 'reçu' stays bare for masculine 'le cadeau', but a feminine noun would force 'reçue'.

target: Après les vacances, il faudra se remettre au travail.
english: After the vacation, we'll have to get back to work.
tip: Il faudra has no real subject – il is a dummy placeholder: il faudra se remettre au travail = 'one will have to' get back to work. It comes from falloir.

target: L'infirmière qui s'occupe de mon père est très gentille.
english: The nurse who takes care of my father is very kind.
tip: S'occuper always needs de for what you handle: qui s'occupe de mon père = who takes care of my father. Drop the de and the sentence breaks.

target: Je ne pourrai pas assister à la réunion de lundi.
english: I won't be able to attend Monday's meeting.
tip: Assister à means to attend, not to assist – a false friend: assister à la réunion = to be at the meeting. To help someone is aider.

target: Lorsque nous aurons vendu la voiture, nous achèterons un vélo.
english: When we've sold the car, we'll buy a bike.
tip: For an action finished before another future one, French uses the future perfect: aurons vendu = will have sold. English just says 'have sold'.

target: Le client qui attend depuis une heure commence à s'impatienter.
english: The customer who has been waiting for an hour is starting to get impatient.
tip: French uses the present with depuis for something still going on: attend depuis une heure = has been waiting for an hour, and still is.

target: Même si j'avais tout l'argent du monde, je ne l'achèterais pas.
english: Even if I had all the money in the world, I wouldn't buy it.
tip: Si never takes a conditional verb – the setup stays imparfait: même si j'avais... je ne l'achèterais pas = even if I had... I wouldn't buy it.

target: Tu verras, tout ira bien.
english: You'll see, everything will be fine.
tip: 'Tu verras' = 'you'll see' is everyday reassurance, not a literal claim about eyesight: 'tu verras, tout ira bien'. Same use as 'on verra' = we'll see.

target: Si tu étudies bien, tu réussiras ton examen.
english: If you study well, you'll pass your exam.
tip: After 'si', French keeps the present even for a future 'if': 'si tu étudies... tu réussiras'. But 'quand' and 'dès que' DO take the future.

target: Si elle avait pris le bus, elle ne serait pas arrivée en retard.
english: If she had taken the bus, she wouldn't have arrived late.
tip: 'arriver' builds its past with 'être', not 'avoir': the would-have form is 'serait arrivée', never 'aurait arrivé'.

target: Nous aurions dû partir plus tôt.
english: We should have left earlier.
tip: English "should have" hides a detour in French: aurions dû is literally "would have had to." Past regret = conditional of devoir + infinitive.

target: Il aurait fallu réserver à l'avance.
english: We should have booked in advance.
tip: 'il aurait fallu' = 'we should have', but names nobody: 'falloir' only ever runs with a dummy 'il' – 'il aurait fallu réserver'.

target: Nul ne croyait qu'il pût survivre.
english: No one believed he could survive.
tip: Nul ne is a bookish "no one," working like personne ne: Nul ne croyait = "no one believed." The ne stays and there's no pas with these negatives.

target: Sans qu'elle le sût, il l'observait.
english: Without her knowing, he was watching her.
tip: Sans que forces the subjunctive: sans qu'elle le sût = "without her knowing." Trigger words like sans que and avant que always pull this mood.

target: Quand tu auras fini tes devoirs, appelle-moi.
english: When you finish your homework, call me.
tip: English says 'when you finish', but French puts the future after 'quand': 'quand tu auras fini' = once you'll have finished.

target: C'est le jour où nous nous sommes rencontrés.
english: It's the day we met.
tip: French uses où (literally "where") for time too: le jour où = "the day when," never "the day where." Same with l'année où and le moment où.

target: La chanson que tu chantes est très belle.
english: The song you're singing is very beautiful.
tip: English can drop the 'that' – 'the song you're singing' – but French can never drop 'que': 'la chanson que tu chantes'.

target: Les voisins qui viennent d'emménager sont très accueillants.
english: The neighbors who just moved in are very welcoming.
tip: Venir de + verb means "just did," not "come to": viennent d'emménager = "just moved in." A present-tense verb covers the recent past.

target: J'avais oublié de fermer la porte en partant.
english: I had forgotten to close the door when leaving.
tip: en + the -ant form means "while/on doing": en partant = "as I was leaving." This is the one spot French uses this gerund shape.

target: Quand nous aurons déjeuné, nous irons nous promener.
english: When we've had lunch, we'll go for a walk.
tip: After quand, French uses the future where English uses the present perfect: nous aurons déjeuné = "when we've had lunch." No present tense here.

target: La fille qui porte un chapeau rouge est ma cousine.
english: The girl wearing a red hat is my cousin.
tip: Color words land after the noun in French: un chapeau rouge, not "un rouge chapeau." Most everyday adjectives follow the noun this way.

target: Ils avaient vendu leur maison avant de déménager à Paris.
english: They had sold their house before moving to Paris.
tip: After avant de, French wants the infinitive, not the -ing form: avant de déménager = "before moving." Same pattern with sans and pour + infinitive.

target: Le pays où il a vécu pendant cinq ans lui manque.
english: He misses the country where he lived for five years.
tip: Manquer flips the subject: lui manque means the country is missing TO him, so HE misses it. The thing missed is the subject; the person is lui, me, te.

target: Si tu avais fait tes devoirs, tu aurais compris la leçon.
english: If you had done your homework, you would have understood the lesson.
tip: The si-half never takes the conditional: si tu avais fait (had done), then tu aurais compris (would have understood). Only the result half gets "would."

target: Je me préparais pour sortir quand tu m'as envoyé un message.
english: I was getting ready to go out when you sent me a message.
tip: Two past tenses split the job: me préparais (imperfect) sets the ongoing scene, tu m'as envoyé (perfect) is the single action that cuts in.

target: Quoiqu'elle eût beaucoup d'argent, elle vivait simplement.
english: Although she had a lot of money, she lived simply.
tip: quoique (one word) = "although"; quoi que (two words) = "whatever." Here quoiqu'elle eût means "although she had," and the verb turns subjunctive.

target: La décision que tu as prise est courageuse.
english: The decision you made is courageous.
tip: "Prise" agrees with "la décision" (feminine singular): pris → prise.

target: C'est un film dont j'ai oublié le titre.
english: It's a movie whose title I've forgotten.
tip: "Dont" replaces possessive "de": le titre du film → dont j'ai oublié le titre.
